newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Vaughan replaces Pringle in NZ squad.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Vaughan replaces Pringle in NZ squad.

text.p: Auckland all-rounder Justin Vaughan was named on Wednesday to replace injured medium-pacer Chris Pringle in the New Zealand cricket team to tour Sharjah and Pakistan next month.
Pringle, who fought his way back into the New Zealand squad with a strong domestic season last summer, has bone spurs on an ankle joint which will require arthroscopic surgery.
He is expected to be out of action for six to eight weeks.
Vaughan, who will join the New Zealand team for their final three-day, pre-tour camp at Lincoln University in Christchurch next week, was considered unlucky to have originally missed the tour party.
The Auckland all-rounder first played for New Zealand when he was one of five replacements on the troubled Sri Lankan tour in 1992.
Vaughan also toured the West Indies earlier this year, being considered one of New Zealand's most consistent and reliable players.
Convenor of selectors Ross Dykes said Pringle had not been troubled by his ankle injury until the last day of the New Zealand team camp in Christchurch last week.
"At the time the injury was not thought to be serious but after consultation with orthopaedic surgeon Stu Walsh, he has been ruled out of touring," said Dykes.
"The team management has consistently said it will not take away any player who is less than 100 percent fit. With this injury, Chris unfortunately would not be able to perform at his best."
Dykes added that Pringle had been disappointed to be ruled out of the tour but the Aucklander had also been adamant that he did not want to let anyone down by performing below his best.
He expects to return to cricket prior to the New Year, which would be in time to press for selection for the two home series against England and Sri Lanka.
